citeinfo.title: High resolution water quality and dissolved carbon data from a coastal Louisiana salt marsh from 2022 to 2023 (ver. 2.0, July 2025)

descript.abstract:
Continuous water quality sensor data were collected at USGS 292939089544400 Wilkinson Bayou cutoff north of Wilkinson Bay, LA gage. Field water quality measurements were collected using a YSI EXO2 water quality sonde equipped with a data logger to capture hourly data using sensors for measuring water temperature, specific conductance, salinity, pH, oxidation and reduction potential (ORP), fluorescent dissolved organic matter (fDOM), turbidity, and dissolved oxygen (DO). The monitor was housed in an 8-inch diameter polyvinyl chloride (PVC) pipe attached to a temporary wooden structure near the gage. Measurements were collected from a fixed mid-depth point in the water column. All data were collected using U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) protocols and data are stored in the National Water Information System (NWIS) database. Records processing of measurement results for fouling and drift corrections of the data followed the USGS Techniques and Methods for continuous water-quality monitors (Wagner et al., 2006), except for ORP and drift corrections for fDOM. ORP were uncorrected and were reported from the sonde directly. fDOM was evaluated for drift using periodic side-by-side comparisons with a new factory-calibrated sensor to check for lamp degradation in the sensor, and calibration checks were performed using on-site prepared fDOM standard. fDOM data have not been corrected for temperature, turbidity, or inner-filter effects (Booth et al., 2023). Turbidity drift corrections were applied using Wagner et al. (2006) except in some cases where it was determined not helpful to apply the correction based on unstable site conditions during the site visit. Sample results from June of 2022 to October 2023 are reported in this data release.
References: Booth, A., Fleck, J., Pellerin, B.A., Hansen, A., Etheridge, A., Foster, G.M., Graham, J.L., Bergamaschi, B.A., Carpenter, K.D., Downing, B.D., Rounds, S.A., and Saraceno, J., 2023, Field techniques for fluorescence measurements targeting dissolved organic matter, hydrocarbons, and wastewater in environmental waters: Principles and guidelines for instrument selection, operation and maintenance, quality assurance, and data reporting: U.S. Geological Survey Techniques and Methods, book 1, chap. D11, 41 p., https://doi.org/10.3133/tm1D11.
Wagner, R.J., Boulger, R.W., Jr., Oblinger, C.J., and Smith, B.A., 2006, Guidelines and standard procedures for continuous water-quality monitors—Station operation, record computation, and data reporting: U.S. Geological Survey Techniques and Methods 1–D3, 51 p. + 8 attachments; accessed August 3, 2022, at https://pubs.usgs.gov/tm/2006/tm1D3/pdf/TM1D3.pdf.

attracc.attraccr: Water-quality attributes in this data release were quality assured for accuracy and consistency using USGS guidelines and standard procedures described in Wagner and others (2006). Water quality sensors are cleaned and checked between field deployments and if needed are calibrated with laboratory standards. In addition, sensors are periodically replaced or repaired based on signal diagnostics. The sonde data results are inspected for errors and corrections for signal drift and fouling are applied to the dataset using methods described in Wagner and others (2006).

dataqual.logic: Water-quality attributes in this data release were checked for duplication, omission, and general outliers and values appear to be within normal ranges expected for the deployment location. Measurement values that did not meet USGS guidelines were deleted or flagged dependent on the degree of discrepancy from the guidelines.
dataqual.complete: The dataset is composed of continuous hourly water-quality sensor measurement data from one location located at the USGS 292939089544400 Wilkinson Bayou cutoff north of Wilkinson Bay, LA gage. Some periods of record between June 2022 and October 2023 are missing and a data gap exists during times when equipment malfunction, weather, or other circumstance did not allow for the continuous collection of sensor data.

horizpa.horizpar: Horizontal and vertical accuracy of water quality data collection was dependent on the deployment structure which housed the sonde. The structure is not expected to move in the horizontal or vertical direction although slight changes in position could occur over time. The sonde was placed at mid-depth on the structure in the same horizontal and vertical locations on the structure during the entire period of record presented in this data release. The resultant dataset represents the water quality measurements and changes associated with changing water levels at the location.
